result.instructions: BIMCraft is a BIM modeler, a Revit-class building model. Lengths are millimetres; x east, y north, z up; the model starts with Level 1 (0) and Level 2 (3000). Model with execute: wall {points: [[0,0],[8000,0],[8000,6000],[0,6000]], closed: true}, door {at: [2000, 0]}, window {at: [8000, 3000]}, room {point: [4000, 3000], name: "Living"}, floor {} (open over a loop of walls standing free inside), roof {} (on Level 2, over the walls below, hipped, open over a loop of them standing free inside; gables: [1, 3] stands those edges upright; slopes: [30, 45, 30, 45] gives each edge its own slope; courtyards: [[[x,y],…]] slopes it round holes in it too), dormer {host: <roof id>, at: [4000, 800]} (on its slope), column {at: [4000, 3000]}, stair {start: [1000, 1000], end: [1000, 2000], railings: true} (with landings: [{at: 8, turn: -90}], it turns right after 8 risers), ramp {start: [-5000, 0], height: 600}, dimension {refs: [[0, 3000], [8000, 3000]], at: [4000, -1000]} (between the walls under those points), tag {} (every door and window); or send several at once with script, one `command {json}` per line. list_commands shows every command and its parameters, and the menu it sits in. Check your work with inspect_model and query_elements, look at it with render (a PNG of a level's plan, with ceiling: true its reflected ceiling plan, of a section or elevation by name, or of the 3D view with view "{3D}"; or a family alone with family, type and mode "3d", "plan" or "elevation" — which draws in no project of yours), and save to .bimc or .ifc.
